beats.text: The first game of its kind was an arcade cabinet called Blockade, made by Gremlin in 1976.
beats.note: It was a two player game where the player who survived longest won. It was written by Lane Hauck and Ago Kiss.

beats.lead: Home computers had it twenty years earlier
beats.text: Worm for the TRS-80, by Peter Trefonas in 1978, is the first known home computer version.
beats.note: MS-DOS then shipped a QBasic version called Nibbles from 1991.

beats.name: Taneli Armanto
beats.role: Nokia design engineer who adapted Snake for its phones. It arrived on the Nokia 6110, the first Nokia phone with Snake pre-installed.

beats.context: Between Blockade in 1976 and Snake on the Nokia 6110 in 1998.

beats.text: Nokia did not invent Snake. It gave it a phone.
